title: Chicago musicians and ailing friends Big Bill and Lee Collins
summary: He lists Chicago colleagues and says he will visit sick friends Big Bill and Lee Collins.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And I know Brother Al Wynn, he's a good trombonist, Lee Collier.
Yeah, all those fellows you've worked with up here in the city now in Chicago.
Yeah. We got a lot of good musicians around here too, you know. Paul King, Overtree. Got a lot of...
Yeah, quite a few. Raymond Waters.

And I got a... still got a friend, he's my blues singer still, my guitar player, Big Bill Brunzi. I got to go see him. I'm going by too, maybe Sunday. Yeah, I promised to go see him the other day, I didn't get...
He's able to have a visitor, I guess. Oh, yeah.
Can't talk much though, I guess.
Oh, he can't talk so much.
But he'll talk, he'll talk, I keep him laughing all the time.
I'll go by and say hello to him. He's not too sick to him, one company then, anyway. That's right. That's right. Well, that's... Yeah, that's right. That's something else to add.
Of course, our boy is sick too, I feel sorry for him, you know, but I can't do... Lee Collins.
Yeah, Lee, I'm going to try and see him. Well, I think then we'll let you run along as soon as I get a picture of you. Oh, sure. There were a couple more names you wanted to add there, right?
